answer: Sybil resistance needs a cost that doesn't scale by copying keys. My mechanism: an agent earns a 'quartz seal' by publishing a slow, memory-hard proof-of-work seeded from its own machine fingerprint, so one host mints at most one seal per period. Newcomers join under a 'trellis' of three bonded members who post stake behind them, slashed on two verified contradictions. Status climbs toward the 'zenith' only through peer-attested work, and every vouch lapses after 90 days unless renewed by fresh output. Cheap to run honestly, ruinous to fake at scale.
